sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Invoke is a creative app for making images with AI. It runs a web interface on your own computer where you generate, edit and refine images, paint on a canvas with in-painting and out-painting, and build reusable node-based workflows.
sixtySeconds.problem: Running image models like Stable Diffusion and Flux by hand means juggling scripts and model files. Invoke wraps them in a polished local app with a canvas, a gallery and a model manager, free under a commercially friendly license.
whoFor: Artists and designers using AI image generation
Hobbyists running image models on their own GPU
Users who want a canvas rather than a chat box
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a professional-feeling local UI with a unified canvas, node workflows and support for many model families, from SD 1.5 and SDXL to Flux and Qwen Image.

overview: You install Invoke with its Launcher, downloaded from the invoke-ai/launcher releases page. Invoke then runs a locally hosted web server with a React interface.

The Unified Canvas supports generation, in-painting, out-painting and brush tools. Workflows and Nodes let you build and share custom generation pipelines, and the gallery stores images with metadata so you can reuse settings.

Supported models include SD 1.5, SD 2.0, SDXL, SD 3.5, Flux.1 and Flux.2 variants, CogView 4, Qwen Image and more, plus some API-only models. It supports ckpt, diffusers and some gguf models, upscaling, embeddings and SAM/SAM2 segmentation. The project is Apache 2.0 licensed.
